evals.name: saas-platform-from-description
evals.prompt:
Create an interactive architecture canvas for our e-commerce platform Shoply — a single self-contained HTML file I can pan/zoom and click around to explore, dark theme. Here's the architecture:

People: shoppers (web + mobile), merchants (dashboard), and support agents. Product surfaces (ours, Next.js): the Storefront, the Merchant Dashboard, and an Admin Console. Core domain services we own: the Catalog service (products, variants, inventory pointers), the Order Orchestrator (saga-based checkout: cart → payment → fulfillment), and the Pricing Engine (promotions, tax, currency). Platform abstractions we own over swappable vendors: PaymentGateway (wraps Stripe and Adyen — card data never touches our services), SearchService (wraps Algolia — indexes the catalog), and Notifier (wraps SendGrid + Twilio for email/SMS). Infra everything runs on: Kubernetes for the services, Postgres for orders + catalog, Kafka as the event bus (order events fan out to search indexing, notifications, and analytics), Redis for carts and sessions. Key flows: shoppers hit the storefront which talks to catalog/pricing/orders; the orchestrator calls PaymentGateway; every order state change lands on Kafka; the analytics pipeline feeds a sales dashboard the merchants see — that's our feedback loop.

Save it to {OUTDIR}/shoply-canvas/index.html. Don't publish anywhere — local file only.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained interactive canvas HTML in the established style: layered bands (humans / product / domain / platform / infra), dashed-vs-solid ownership semantics, orthogonal labeled edges including the Kafka fan-out and analytics feedback loop, pan/zoom + click-to-isolate + readout.
assertions: index.html exists at the requested path and is fully self-contained (no references to local files; only network assets like Google Fonts allowed)
The inline JavaScript is syntactically valid (the page can execute without parse errors)
Interactive pan and zoom: the page wires pointer-drag panning and wheel/pinch zooming
Click-to-inspect: clicking (or hovering) a component reveals a name + description readout for that component
Dark theme: page background is a dark color
Layered-band composition: the diagram groups components into horizontal layer zones (bands/planes), not a free-form node graph
Ownership semantics encoded in line style: owned/in-house abstractions rendered with dashed borders, vendor/swappable infra with solid borders
All core components appear: Storefront, Merchant Dashboard, Catalog, Order Orchestrator, Pricing Engine, PaymentGateway, SearchService, Notifier, Kafka, Postgres, Redis, Kubernetes
The analytics → merchant/sales-dashboard feedback loop is drawn as an explicit edge (not just mentioned in text)
Kafka fan-out is visible: order events flow to at least search indexing and notifications

evals.name: ml-pipeline-from-description
evals.prompt: we're presenting our ML platform 'meridian' to the new platform team next week. can you build an interactive architecture diagram i can explore (pan/zoom, click things for details)? dark mode please. here's how it works: raw events land in S3 via Kinesis Firehose, and batch dumps arrive nightly from the warehouse (Snowflake). our Ingestion Gateway (ours) validates + normalizes everything into the lake. the Feature Store is our own abstraction on top of Redis (online) and S3/parquet (offline). training: Airflow schedules jobs, our Training Orchestrator (ours) runs them on EKS GPU nodes, artifacts + lineage go to MLflow. the Model Registry wrapper (ours) gates promotion — a model can't ship without passing our Eval Harness (ours, runs golden datasets). serving: our Inference Gateway (ours) fronts Triton servers on EKS, does canary routing + feature lookup. monitoring: predictions + outcomes stream back through Kinesis into the Drift Monitor (ours) which can trigger retraining via Airflow — that closed loop is the whole point of the platform. save to {OUTDIR}/meridian-canvas/index.html. no need to publish it anywhere.
evals.expected_output: An explorable canvas showing the ML lifecycle as layered planes (sources → ingestion → features/training → registry/eval gate → serving → monitoring) with the drift-monitor retraining feedback loop routed as a long gutter edge, owned abstractions dashed vs AWS/vendor infra solid.
assertions: index.html exists at the requested path and is fully self-contained (no references to local files; only network assets like Google Fonts allowed)
The inline JavaScript is syntactically valid (the page can execute without parse errors)
Interactive pan and zoom: the page wires pointer-drag panning and wheel/pinch zooming
Click-to-inspect: clicking (or hovering) a component reveals a name + description readout for that component
Dark theme: page background is a dark color
Layered-band composition: the diagram groups components into horizontal layer zones (bands/planes), not a free-form node graph
Ownership semantics encoded in line style: owned/in-house abstractions rendered with dashed borders, vendor/swappable infra with solid borders

All owned components appear and are distinguishable from vendor infra: Ingestion Gateway, Feature Store, Training Orchestrator, Model Registry, Eval Harness, Inference Gateway, Drift Monitor vs S3, Kinesis, Snowflake, Airflow, EKS, MLflow, Redis, Triton
The closed retraining loop is drawn: monitoring/Drift Monitor routes back to Airflow/training as an explicit edge
The eval gate is in the promotion path: Eval Harness sits between training artifacts and serving/registry promotion
